segments.arabic:
١٢١٠٢- أم شريك:
الدّوسيّة «١» . ذكرها يونس بن بكير في رواية السّيرة عن أبي إسحاق، فقال يونس عن عبد الأعلى بن أبي المساور، عن محمد بن عمر بن عطاء، عن أبي هريرة، قال: كانت امرأة من دوس يقال لها أم شريك أسلمت في رمضان فأقبلت تطلب من يصحبها إلى رسول اللَّه ﵌، فلقيت رجلا من اليهود، فقال: ما لك يا أم شريك؟ قالت: أطلب من يصحبني إلى النّبيّ ﵌. قال: تعالى، فأنا أصحبك ... وذكر الحديث بطوله.
وأخرجه ابن سعد، من طريق يحيى بن سعيد الأنصاريّ مرسلا، قال: هاجرت أم شريك الدّوسيّة فصحبت يهوديّا في الطريق، فأمست صائمة، فقال اليهودي لامرأته: لئن سقيتها لأفعلنّ، فباتت كذلك حتى إذا كان في آخر اللّيل إذا على صدرها دلو موضوع وصفن، فشربت منه، ثم بعثتهم للدلجة، فقال اليهوديّ، إني لأسمع صوت امرأة، لقد شربت، فقالت: لا، واللَّه إن سقيتني. قال: والصّفن، بفتح المهملة والفاء، مثل الجراب أو المزود.
وسيأتي لها قصّة أخرى في التي بعدها.
قال الواقديّ: الثّبت عندنا أنّ الواهبة امرأة من دوس بن الأزد عرضت نفسها على النّبيّ ﷺ، وكانت جميلة وقد أسنّت، فقالت: إني أهب نفسي لك
(١) أسد الغابة ت (٧٤٩٦) .
segments.english:
12102—Umm Sharik:

The Dawsiyya.¹ Yunus ibn Bukayr mentioned her in his transmission of al-Sira from Abu Ishaq. Yunus related from Abd al-Ala ibn Abi al-Musawir, from Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Ata, from Abu Hurayra, who said: There was a woman of Daws called Umm Sharik. She embraced Islam during Ramadan and set out seeking someone to accompany her to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. She met a Jewish man, who asked, “What is the matter, Umm Sharik?” She replied, “I am seeking someone to accompany me to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.” He said, “Come; I shall accompany you.” He then related the hadith in full.

Ibn Sa'd also transmitted it by way of Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Ansari as a mursal report. He said: Umm Sharik al-Dawsiyya emigrated and accompanied a Jewish man on the road. Evening came while she was fasting. The Jewish man said to his wife, “If you give her water, I shall surely deal with you.” She remained in that condition until, near the end of the night, she found a bucket placed upon her chest, together with a safan. She drank from it. Then she woke them for the night march. The Jewish man said, “I can hear a woman’s voice; you have surely drunk!” She replied, “No, by Allah; you did not give me anything to drink.” The word safan, with the undotted sad and the fa both bearing a fatha, means something like a sack or a provision bag.

Another account concerning her will appear in the entry immediately following this one.

Al-Waqidi said: The firmly established report according to us is that the woman who offered herself was a woman of Daws ibn al-Azd. She offered herself to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. She was beautiful but had grown old, and she said, “I give myself to you—

¹ Usd al-Ghaba, entry 7496.

segments.arabic: وأتصدّق بها عليك فقبلها. فقالت عائشة: ما في المرأة تهب نفسها لرجل خير. فقالت أم شريك: هي أنا، فنزلت: وَامْرَأَةً مُؤْمِنَةً إِنْ وَهَبَتْ نَفْسَها لِلنَّبِيِّ [الأحزاب: ٥٠] . قال الواقديّ: رأيت من عندنا يقول: إن هذه الآية نزلت في أمّ شريك.
segments.english: “and make a charitable gift of myself to you.” He accepted her. Aisha said, “There is no good in a woman who gives herself to a man.” Umm Sharik said, “I am that woman.” Then the following was revealed: “And a believing woman, if she offers herself to the Prophet” [al-Ahzab 33:50]. al-Waqidi said: I saw one of our people say that this verse was revealed concerning Umm Sharik.

unresolved.arabic_span: إذا على صدرها دلو موضوع وصفن، فشربت منه
unresolved.explanation: The Arabic coordinates a bucket and a safan but does not establish their precise physical relationship or make the antecedent of “from it” fully explicit. The final English deliberately retains this ambiguity.

unresolved.arabic_span: إني لأسمع صوت امرأة، لقد شربت
unresolved.explanation: The unvocalized شربت can mean either “you have drunk” or “she has drunk.” The final text retains the second-person reading because it produces a direct exchange with Umm Sharik, but the supplied witnesses do not conclusively exclude the third-person reading.
